questions.stem: The histogram in Figure 1 shows the time taken, to the nearest minute, for 140 runners to complete a fun run.

parts.text:
Use the histogram to calculate the number of runners who took between 78.5 and 90.5 minutes to complete the fun run.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
Width: 1, 1, 4, 2, 3, 5, 3, 12; Freq. Density: 6, 7, 2, 6, 5.5, 2, 1.5, 0.5 M1: for attempt at width of the correct bar (90.5-78.5) [may be on histogram or in table]
A1: $0.5\times 12$ or $6$ (may be seen on the histogram; must be related to the area of the bar above 78.5-90.5)
Total area is $(1\times 6)+(1\times 7)+(4\times 2)+\ldots = 70$ M1: for attempting area of correct bar $\times \frac{140}{\text{their } 70}$
$(90.5-78.5)\times \frac{1}{2}\times \frac{140}{\text{their } 70}$ B1: "70 seen anywhere" in their working
Number of runners is 12 A1: for correct answer of 12
(5)
Notes: Minimum working required is $2\times 0.5\times 12$ where the 2 should come from $\frac{140}{70}$. Beware $90.5-78.5=12$ (this scores M1A0M0B0A0). Common answer is $0.5\times 12=6$ (this scores M1A1M0B0A0). If unsure send to review e.g. $2\times 0.5\times 12=12$ without 70 being seen.

questions.stem:
The following shows the results of a wine tasting survey of 100 people.

96 like wine $A$,
93 like wine $B$,
96 like wine $C$,
92 like $A$ and $B$,
91 like $B$ and $C$,
93 like $A$ and $C$,
90 like all three wines.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Draw a Venn Diagram to represent these data.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
Diagram may be drawn with $B\subset (A\cup C)$ or with the 0 for $B\cap (A\cup C)'$ simply left blank.
M1: for 3 closed, labelled curves that overlap
A1: for the 90, 3, 2 and 1 (3cc correctly placed)
M1: for one of 1, 0 or 2 correct, or a correct sum of 4 values for $A$, $B$ or $C$
A1: for all 7 values correct (accept a blank instead of 0)
B1: for the 1 outside the box
(6)
Notes: Final mark is a B1 for the box not an A mark. In parts (b) to (f) full marks can be scored for correct answers or correct ft. Accept decimals or probabilities in the Venn diagram.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Find the probability that a randomly selected person from the survey likes

(b) none of the three wines,
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
P(none) = 0.01 B1ft: follow through their '1' from outside divided by 100
(1)

parts.label: c
parts.mark_scheme:
P($A$ but not $B$) = 0.04
M1: for correct expression e.g. P($A\cup B$) $-$ P($B$) or calculation e.g. 3+1 or 4 on top
A1: for a correct probability, follow through their '3+1' from diagram
(2)
Notes: For M marks in (c) to (e) they must have a fraction.

parts.label: d
parts.text:
(d) any wine in the survey except wine $C$,
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
P(any wine but $C$) = 0.03
M1: for correct expression or calculation e.g. 1+2+0 or 99-96 or 3 on top
A1: for a correct probability, follow through their '2+1+0' from diagram
(2)

parts.label: e
parts.text:
(e) exactly two of the three kinds of wine.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
P(exactly two) = 0.06
M1: for a correct expression or calculation e.g. 3+2+1 or 6 on top
A1: for a correct probability, follow through their values from diagram
(2)

parts.label: f
parts.text:
Given that a person from the survey likes wine $A$,

(f) find the probability that the person likes wine $C$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
P($C|A$) = $\frac{\mathrm{P}(C\cap A)}{\mathrm{P}(A)} = \frac{93}{96}$ or $\frac{31}{32}$ or AWRT 0.969
M1: for a correct expression up to "," and some correct substitution, ft their values. One of these probabilities must be correct or correct ft. If P($C$) on bottom, M0
A1ft: follow through their $A\cap C$ and their $A$ but the ratio must be in (0, 1)
A1: for correct answer only. Answer only scores 3/3, but check working: P($A\cap C$)/P($C$) is M0
(3)
Total 16 marks

questions.stem: The weights of bags of popcorn are normally distributed with mean of 200 g and 60% of all bags weighing between 190 g and 210 g.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Write down the median weight of the bags of popcorn.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
200 or 200 g B1
(1)
Notes: "mean = 200 g" is B0 but "median = 200" or just "200" alone is B1.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find the standard deviation of the weights of the bags of popcorn.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
P($190<X<210$) = 0.6 or P($X<210$) = 0.8 or P($X>210$) = 0.2 or diagram (o.e.) M1
Correct use of 0.8 or 0.2 A1
$Z = (\pm)\frac{210-200}{\sigma}$ M1
$\frac{10}{\sigma} = 0.8416$ B1: for $z=0.8416$ (or better) [$z=0.84$ usually just loses this mark in (a)]
$\sigma = 11.882129\ldots$ AWRT 11.9 A1
(5)
Notes: Standardization in (b) and (c). They must use $\sigma$ not $\sigma^2$ or $\sqrt{\sigma}$. 1st M1 for a correct probability statement (as given or e.g. P($200<X<210$)=0.3 o.e.) or shaded diagram - must have values on z-axis and probability areas shown. 1st A1 for correct use of 0.8 or $p=0.2$. Need a correct probability statement. May be implied by a suitable value for $z$ seen (e.g. $z=0.84$). 2nd M1 for attempting to standardise. Values for $x$ and $\mu$ used in formula. Don't need $z=$ for this M1 nor a $z$-value, just mark standardization. 2nd A1 for AWRT 11.9.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
A shopkeeper finds that customers will complain if their bag of popcorn weighs less than 180 g.

(c) Find the probability that a customer will complain.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
P($X<180$) = P$\left(Z<\frac{180-200}{\sigma}\right)$ M1: for attempting to standardise with 200 and their $\sigma>0$ e.g. $(\pm)\frac{180-200}{\text{their }\sigma}$
= P($Z<-1.6832$) M1: for $1-$ a probability from tables provided, compatible with their probability statement [NB on epen this is an A mark, ignore and treat it as 2nd M1]
$=1-0.9535$
$=0.0465$ or AWRT 0.046 A1: for 0.0465 or AWRT 0.046 (dependent on both Ms in part (c))
(3)
Total 9 marks
